Regulatory Transformation

Regulatory Transformation: navigating emerging risks, driving AI adoption and reducing regulatory burden

Regulators are facing a shifting operating environment as technology, markets, environmental pressures and societal expectations evolve faster than traditional regulatory frameworks. Fragmented data and limited intelligence continue to make risk prioritisation difficult.

There is a growing opportunity to use advanced analytics to better target regulatory effort. Many regulators are still working to integrate data across systems, uplift analytical capability and embed insights into everyday decision-making.

AI adoption is also becoming a core regulatory transformation issue. Regulators are seeking to balance opportunities for automation and improved risk identification with the need to manage governance, transparency, bias, legal risk, privacy and public confidence.

At the same time, governments are under pressure to reduce red tape, make faster decisions and manage fiscal constraints. This is driving interest in regulatory consolidation, shared-service models and more consistent approaches to regulatory delivery, while maintaining fairness and strong outcomes.

Regulation Hub Intelligence Brief

AI Brief 134 articles across 8 categories

The fortnight is shaped by three converging regulator investment themes: digital safety and AI enforcement capability expansion, with eSafety activating legislated $99 million platform penalties and the AFP laying Australia's first AI-generated CSAM charges while WA Police faces governance backlash over live facial recognition deployment; AML/CTF regime extension, with AUSTRAC simultaneously publishing designated-service guidance for real estate agents, insolvency practitioners, and jewellers — a structural compliance onboarding mandate across three previously unregulated sectors; and transport infrastructure investment, anchored by Queensland Budget rail expansion funding and ETCS convergence emerging as a multi-year national signalling program requiring immediate program advisory pre-positioning. HSBC's $35 million ASIC scam-protection penalty and Binance's AUSTRAC-driven global compliance overhaul are the financial services client signals this cycle, each generating peer-institution mandates across the regulated banking and digital-asset cohort. In education, TEQSA's paired AI governance publications combined with a high-profile resignation citing regulator overreach confirm a hardening enforcement posture that university clients are structurally ill-equipped to navigate without external advisory support. Queensland Government, Transport for NSW, major ADIs, digital platform operators, TEQSA-registered providers, and the newly designated AUSTRAC sectors represent the priority near-term client engagement targets. KPMG must mobilise transport advisory to pre-position on Queensland rail procurement, activate the AML/CTF practice for the AUSTRAC-designated sector rollout, brief financial services clients on ASIC enforcement posture, and bring an AI governance offer to market for law enforcement and higher education clients before H2 2026 budget cycles close.

Cross-category themes

A consistent enforcement escalation is underway across virtually every regulatory domain — from ASIC's record penalties and AUSTRAC's tranche-two mobilisation to TEQSA, AMSA, and the ESC tightening compliance postures simultaneously — signalling that regulators across Australia are moving from guidance to active prosecution in a coordinated shift that will compress client response timelines. Overlaid on this enforcement acceleration are structural reform pipelines — new governance standards, expanded regulator mandates, mandatory registration regimes, and emerging AI and geopolitical risk obligations — that together represent a sustained, cross-sector compliance uplift cycle and a material advisory opportunity for KPMG across gap assessments, frameworks design, and regulator engagement strategy.

APRA is running a dual-track enforcement agenda this fortnight: a formal governance overhaul imposing board-level accountability obligations on all regulated entities, and a geopolitical-risk preparedness directive putting banks on a war footing alongside the RBA — two distinct mandates that will hit the same board and executive committees simultaneously and create immediate demand for independent assurance over both frameworks. ASIC is enforcing hard on private credit ahead of 30 June valuations and reporting deadlines, with REP 832 on car loans signalling that credit-product governance is next in the review queue; the Owenell auditor registration surrender underscores that assurance independence is under active scrutiny, raising the bar for any entity relying on connected audit arrangements. AUSTRAC has materially expanded the AML/CTF designated-services perimeter to cover real estate agents and insolvency practitioners — two sectors with no mature compliance infrastructure — while the Binance probe being adopted as a global overhaul template confirms AUSTRAC is setting international enforcement architecture, not just domestic sanctions. ATSB's final report on the Cloncurry ore train collision and Comcare's safety undertaking against the Royal Australian Mint indicate active safety-assurance demand in federal government operations and heavy-industry rail, sectors where formal undertaking compliance milestones will drive structured advisory mandates. TEQSA's simultaneous release of gen-AI assurance guidance and a self-assurance report framework for new providers signals that higher-education assurance is being structurally reset, creating a repeatable advisory offer across registration cohorts. Across all five regulatory fronts — APRA, ASIC, AUSTRAC, Comcare/ATSB, TEQSA — the common thread is regulators converting policy intent into board-level accountability and compliance infrastructure gaps that KPMG's Risk, Regulation, and Internal Audit capabilities are best placed to fill.

State-gov priorities

Cited strategic priorities across all 9 jurisdictions, refreshed bi-annually. Every source URL is .gov.au.

Housing supply is the single most universal cross-jurisdiction priority, with every state and territory committing to ambitious dwelling targets — VIC's 800,000-home decade plan, QLD's 1 million homes by 2046, NSW's 170,000+ TOD pipeline, TAS's 10,000 affordable homes, and ACT's 30,000-home target — creating consistent demand for planning reform advisory, delivery sequencing, and program assurance. An industrial policy convergence is simultaneously evident, with the Commonwealth's $22.7B Future Made in Australia, NSW's onshoring of energy and rollingstock manufacturing, WA's $1B Strategic Industries Fund, SA's State Prosperity Project in critical minerals and green manufacturing, and QLD's 30-year Resources Industry Development Plan all signalling a coordinated pivot toward sovereign economic resilience. Renewable energy and net zero transition is a near-universal commitment — SA targets 100% net renewable electricity by 2027, TAS aims for 200% generation by 2040, and ACT pursues net zero by 2045 — yet NT stands structurally apart, explicitly prioritising mining, conventional energy, agriculture, and resource extraction as its primary growth levers, reflecting a divergence between resource-dependent northern economies and southern states leading the energy transition. Defence investment is an emerging cross-jurisdictional cluster, with the Commonwealth's $330B Integrated Investment Program anchoring a broader industrial ecosystem that WA's Defence West 2025–2040 strategy and NT's defence-sector budget prioritisation are both actively positioning to capture. Public sector reform and long-horizon governance frameworks appear consistently — the Commonwealth's APS Reform Agenda (59 initiatives, Public Service Amendment Act 2024), SA's 20-Year Infrastructure Strategy, WA's Infrastructure WA framework, and ACT's Wellbeing Budget integration all reflect shared appetite for evidence-based, institutionally durable governance. Law and order diverges sharply along political lines: NT's Crime Reduction Strategy and QLD's Making Queensland Safer Act reflect a punitive reform agenda largely absent from ACT, VIC, and Commonwealth priorities, creating distinct program design and evaluation contexts across jurisdictions. For KPMG PEPI, the highest-density BD opportunities lie in housing delivery assurance where execution risk is high and timelines are compressed across all jurisdictions, energy transition commercialisation and hydrogen investment facilitation at the SA–TAS–Commonwealth nexus, APS and public sector capability uplift aligned to the Commonwealth's four reform pillars, and defence industry strategy support in WA and NT where sovereign industrial ecosystems are being built from policy intent to investable programs.

Last refreshed 2026-05-20. Bi-annual schedule; source URLs verified to .gov.au.

Commonwealth

  • Future Made in Australia
    The Treasury / Department of Industry, Science and Resources 2024-2034 (10-year, $22.7B package)
    Program design, sector assessment frameworks, investment mandate design, industry consultation, economic modelling, community benefit evaluation
    Source (2024-05-14)
  • Strengthening Medicare
    Department of Health, Disability and Ageing 2023-2027 (reform rolling); Budget 2025-26 expansion from Nov 2025
    Primary care reform evaluation, Urgent Care Clinic rollout support, workforce modelling, digital health implementation, Medicare integrity assurance
    Source (2024-05-14)
  • 2024 National Defence Strategy and Integrated Investment Program
    Department of Defence 2024-2034 ($330B Integrated Investment Program to 2033-34)
    Capability program assurance, workforce strategy, sovereign industrial capability priorities, AUKUS implementation support, capability reviews
    Source (2024-04-17)
  • APS Reform Agenda
    Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet / Australian Public Service Commission 2022-ongoing (4 pillars, 59 initiatives; Public Service Amendment Act 2024 enacted)
    Integrity and capability reviews, workforce strategy, stewardship framework design, data & digital workforce planning, contractor-to-APS conversion support
    Source (2024-12-01)
  • Working for Women: A Strategy for Gender Equality
    Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (Office for Women) 2024-2034 (10-year strategy)
    Gender impact analysis, workplace gender equality evaluation, Government Board appointment strategy support, pay-gap economic modelling, consultation design
    Source (2024-03-07)
  • Aged Care reform – transition to Support at Home
    Department of Health, Disability and Ageing Aged Care Act 2024 commenced 1 Nov 2025; CHSP transition to Support at Home by 1 Jul 2027
    Provider transition support, data and digital strategy implementation, workforce modelling, single assessment system evaluation, consumer journey design
    Source (2024-07-01)

New South Wales

  • Safe Staffing Levels in NSW public hospitals
    NSW Ministry of Health Phase one early 2024; full rollout 2,480 FTE nurses/midwives by June 2027
    Workforce modelling, implementation assurance, change management support, clinical governance advisory, rostering system review
    Source (2024-03-11)
  • Transport Oriented Development Program (TOD)
    Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure TOD planning controls commenced 13 May 2024; 15-year horizon; 170,000+ homes
    Precinct planning, inclusionary zoning advisory, infrastructure funding strategy, development feasibility, stakeholder consultation
    Source (2024-05-13)
  • Sydney Metro – Western Sydney Airport and Sydney Metro West
    Transport for NSW / Sydney Metro Western Sydney Airport line opens 2026; Metro West completion by 2032; network to 46 stations by 2030
    Program assurance, capability reviews, cost estimation reviews, land use integration, precinct economic analysis
    Source (2024-06-01)
  • Bringing back manufacturing to NSW (state-owned energy and rollingstock)
    Cabinet Office / Treasury NSW / Transport for NSW 2023-2027+ (current Parliament)
    Industrial strategy advisory, local content analysis, state-owned corporation establishment, procurement strategy, workforce development
    Source (2024-09-01)
  • NSW Budget 2025-26 priorities (essential services + diversified economy)
    NSW Treasury 2025-26 forward estimates to 2028-29
    Fiscal strategy advisory, expenditure review, program evaluation, revenue analysis, investment prioritisation
    Source (2025-06-24)
  • Safer Pathway – domestic and family violence response
    Department of Communities and Justice Statewide rollout ongoing; DFV reforms 2024-ongoing
    Service design, outcomes evaluation, risk assessment framework review, cross-agency data sharing advisory, program logic review
    Source (2024-01-01)

Victoria

  • Victoria's Housing Statement – The Decade Ahead 2024-2034
    Department of Transport and Planning 2024-2034 (800,000 homes / 80,000 per year target)
    Planning reform advisory, activity centre masterplans, affordable housing economics, surplus land unlocking, stakeholder consultation, LGA target negotiations
    Source (2023-09-20)
  • Plan for Victoria (long-term plan to 2051)
    Department of Transport and Planning Released Feb 2025; horizon to 2051 (2.24 million homes target)
    LGA housing target analysis, settlement pattern modelling, sustainability and climate policy integration, First Peoples self-determination in planning, infrastructure sequencing
    Source (2025-02-01)
  • Mental Health and Wellbeing reform (Royal Commission implementation)
    Department of Health 2021-2031 (decade of reform); Statewide Service and Capital Plan 2024-2037
    Service design, capital planning, workforce strategy, outcomes evaluation, lived experience engagement design, Mental Health Levy economic analysis
    Source (2024-07-01)
  • Treaty for Victoria / First Peoples' self-determination
    First Peoples – State Relations Statewide Treaty Bill 2025 introduced; negotiations ongoing
    Closing the Gap accountability framework design, service commissioning transition, policy impact analysis, governance advisory for new representative body
    Source (2025-02-01)
  • Breakthrough Victoria Fund – research and innovation commercialisation
    Department of Jobs, Skills, Industry and Regions 2020-2030 ($2B 10-year fund; $1.3B co-investment leveraged by 2024)
    Commercialisation strategy, innovation ecosystem review, investment thesis advisory, co-investment deal structuring, industry sector analysis
    Source (2024-06-30)

Queensland

  • Making Queensland Safer – adult crime, adult time youth justice reform
    Department of Youth Justice and Victim Support (renamed 1 Nov 2024) Making Queensland Safer Act 2024 assented 13 Dec 2024; Queensland Youth Justice Strategy 2024-2028
    Program logic review, early intervention evaluation, victim advocacy service design, circuit breaker sentencing assurance, regional reset program evaluation

  • Homes for Queenslanders housing plan

  • A Fresh Start – cost-of-living and tax relief

  • Queensland Resources Industry Development Plan (QRIDP)

  • Bruce Highway Advisory Council and regional infrastructure

  • Department of the Premier and Cabinet Strategic Plan 2024-2028
    Department of the Premier and Cabinet (Queensland) 2024-2028 (current through 30 April 2025 review; superseded by 2025-2029 plan)

Western Australia

  • WA Government Priorities 2025-2029 (Jobs, Health, Housing, Community, Environment, Infrastructure and Services)
    Department of the Premier and Cabinet (WA) 2025-2029 (current parliamentary term)

  • Made in WA Plan – $1B Strategic Industries Fund

  • Defence West: WA Defence and Defence Industry Strategy 2025

  • Diversify WA: 2024 Update (economic development framework)

  • State Prosperity Project

  • South Australia's Net Zero Strategy 2024-2030
